hypothesis: Repeat Round 1's exact default-Inductor configuration with the persistent compile cache already populated to determine whether the frozen total_s metric benefits after cold compilation is removed. This is a confirmation/retry, not a genuinely different plateau hypothesis.

provenance.implementation: Same isolated SANA_ENABLE_COMPILE=1 setting as Round 1, with the worktree-local persistent Inductor/Triton cache populated by Round 1.

build.note: Persistent kernels loaded successfully, but the first in-process compiled invocation still cost 44.40 seconds. The optional DeepGEMM import traceback remained non-fatal.

assessment.tool_limitation: The archived evaluator did not resolve BASELINE-LOCK.json and incorrectly requested lossy quality evidence; overlay kernel gating was applied instead.

validity.method_semantics: Identical to Round 1: default torch.compile changes only equivalent lowering/fusion/scheduling and retains the complete SANA-Video algorithm and logical work.
validity.visual_note: Authenticity-only check passed. All three decoded frame hashes equal the already inspected valid Round 1 frames from the same fixed seed/workload, and the independent MP4/ffprobe contract is valid. No quality comparison was performed.

decision.reason: The hot persistent-cache run still measures 81.6 seconds in the frozen total_s scope, only 0.756x the 61.7-second baseline. Although its post-initialization warmed request is 1.315x faster and peak memory is 4.6% lower, the required single-generation objective includes 44.40 seconds of first-process compiled invocation cost. Default compile is therefore not part of the latency frontier; this repeat does not count toward the distinct-hypothesis plateau counter.
